name: Amman
intro: Jordan's hilltop capital mixes Roman ruins, downtown souqs, galleries and a lively café culture.
history: Built over seven hills, Amman grew from ancient Rabbath-Ammon and a Roman Philadelphia into a modern capital. Its Citadel and Roman Theatre sit above the downtown souqs.

name: Irbid
intro: A university city in the green north, gateway to Umm Qais and its views over the Sea of Galilee and the Golan.
history: The Decapolis city of Gadara stood at today's Umm Qais, famed for its Roman theatre of black basalt.

name: Zarqa
intro: An industrial hub in central Jordan, close to the Azraq oasis and the eastern desert.
history: Zarqa is a modern city, while nearby Azraq has served as a desert crossroads and oasis for centuries.

name: Balqa
intro: Home to the Dead Sea shore and the golden-stone town of As-Salt.
history: As-Salt grew as a trading town and still holds Ottoman-era heritage houses; the Dead Sea lies at Earth's lowest land elevation.

name: Madaba
intro: The City of Mosaics, known for Byzantine floors and views toward Mount Nebo.
history: Madaba's Church of St George holds a 6th-century mosaic map of the Holy Land.

name: Jerash
intro: One of the best-preserved Roman provincial cities in the world.
history: Gerasa flourished as a Decapolis city; its colonnaded street and oval plaza remain remarkably intact.

name: Ajloun
intro: Pine-covered hills, nature reserve trails and a hilltop castle in the green north.
history: Qal'at ar-Rabad was built in the 12th century to guard against Crusader threats and commands wide views.

name: Mafraq
intro: Gateway to the basalt-built Umm al-Jimal and the eastern desert.
history: Umm al-Jimal is a Roman and Byzantine-era town built from black basalt.

name: Karak
intro: Crusader fortress, King's Highway views and hearty mansaf.
history: Karak Castle was among the largest Crusader castles in the region.

name: Tafilah
intro: Home to Dana Biosphere Reserve and deep canyon trails.
history: Dana is Jordan's largest nature reserve, with a stone village on the canyon rim.

name: Ma'an
intro: The governorate of Petra, the Nabataean rose-red city.
history: Petra was the Nabataean capital, carved into sandstone cliffs and entered through the Siq.

name: Aqaba
intro: Jordan's Red Sea coast and the gateway to Wadi Rum.
history: Aqaba has been a port since antiquity; Wadi Rum's red-sand valleys lie nearby.
